source_title: Micron Announces Further Actions to Address Market Conditions
claim_relevant_visible_text: Micron Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: MU), today announced that in response to market conditions, the company is reducing DRAM and NAND wafer starts by approximately 20% versus fiscal fourth quarter 2022. These reductions will be made across all technology nodes where Micron has meaningful output. Micron is also working toward additional capex cuts. In calendar 2023, Micron now expects its year-on-year bit supply growth to be negative for DRAM, and in the single-digit percentage range for NAND. Recently, the market outlook for calendar 2023 has weakened. In order to significantly improve total inventory in the supply chain, Micron believes that in calendar 2023, year-on-year DRAM bit supply will need to shrink and NAND bit supply growth will need to be significantly lower than previous estimates.
researcher_paraphrase: Micron announced an approximately 20% reduction in DRAM and NAND wafer starts and explicitly linked lower future bit supply to improving total supply-chain inventory.
precision_guard: The wafer-start reduction is a Micron action versus its fiscal-Q4-2022 baseline. The future bit-supply statements are management expectations, not realized 2023 industry Outcomes.
authority_boundary: Micron is primary for its own wafer-start action and supply plan, not for competitors' production cuts.
